column1: # The version pins that no Renovate manager moves, each with where it is, why Renovate does not move
# it and how it is moved. scripts/check-renovate-pins fails for a pin that Renovate does not extract
# (.renovate/extracted.tsv) and this list does not hold, for an entry whose pin is not in its file,
# and for an entry that Renovate now extracts or moves with a pin it extracts.
# Columns, separated by tabs: file, a string that names the pin in that file, why, how.

column3: the SHA-256 of the runner's linux-x64 package as the release's notes give it, which setup verifies the package against; it is read from the notes, not computed from the package by a datasource
column4: when Renovate moves actions_runner, set this to the checksum the release's notes give in the same pull request, or ci-host-setup refuses the package (docs/runbooks/ci-host.md)

column3: the engine's image moves with the dagger CLI pin in mise.toml, which has no datasource, so its tag and digest are not moved on their own
column4: set it with the dagger pin: mise.toml's http:dagger version and checksums, engineVersion in .dagger/modules/ci/dagger-module.toml and this image's tag and digest, one release, one pull request

column3: the key of the tools image's inputs, a hash of files and values that no datasource knows
column4: written by just tools-image-pin, together with ci_tools_image (README, The tools image)

column3: the digest of the tools image the tools image workflow published for those inputs, known only after the workflow has run
column4: written by just tools-image-pin <digest> on a branch from main once the image's signature verifies (README, The tools image)

column3: Dagger 1.0 betas are published on dl.dagger.io, not as release assets mise's registry knows, so Renovate has no datasource for the pin; its per-platform checksums change with the version
column4: moved with the dagger_engine pin, as that pin's steps say; the checksums are those of the release's checksums.txt

column3: the engine version the module is built for, which no manager reads and which must be the dagger CLI's
column4: set with the dagger pin in mise.toml, as dagger_engine's steps say

column3: a comment naming the helm-controller release the pinned Flux runs, whose source the code beside it follows
column4: when the flux2 pin moves to a Flux that runs another helm-controller, read the cited source again and update the comment

column3: Renovate's github-actions manager reads the mise-action steps' version as jdx/mise and, with no checksum here, would move it alone, without the workflows whose checksum it cannot look up, which tests/ci.bats refuses, as the publish workflow's mise must be this one's; .renovate/managers.json5 tells it not to propose jdx/mise while the version is written without the v
column4: with the mise version and checksum of the other workflows, as their entries say

column3: Renovate's github-actions manager reads the mise-action step's version and sha256 as jdx/mise; to move the checksum it first fetches the current release by the tag the version is written as, which lacks the v of jdx/mise's release tags, so the lookup fails and Renovate proposes no update (.renovate/tag-forms.tsv), and .renovate/managers.json5 tells it not to propose jdx/mise while the version has that form
column4: in one pull request with the other workflows' mise: the version, and the checksum that the release's SHASUMS256.txt gives for ./mise-v<version>-linux-x64, the binary the action checks (docs/kubernetes.md, Publishing)

column3: a record, in a comment, of the piraeus-operator release whose templates the podTemplates name the containers of, read from the operator's source; tests/pod-security.bats fails while the application runs another
column4: when Renovate moves the piraeus-operator chart to another operator, read its pkg/resources/cluster templates at that version, update the podTemplates and set this record, in the same pull request (the comment above it)

column3: a record, in a comment, of the Kubernetes minor whose Pod Security checks the pinned Kyverno evaluator matches, found by comparing its fork's checks with upstream's; scripts/pod-security-check fails when versions.yaml names a newer minor
column4: when versions.yaml's kubernetes moves to a newer minor, compare that minor's checks with the fork's and move this record, and the http:kyverno pin with it where a newer Kyverno is needed (mise.toml's comment)

column3: Kyverno's CLI from its GitHub releases through mise's http backend, which Renovate's mise manager does not read; its per-platform checksums change with the version, and it stays on the 1.19 line, the last to run the legacy podSecurity rule the check uses; nothing flags a new 1.19.x patch release
column4: with the pod-security-evaluator-covers record, as mise.toml's comment says: the version and the checksums that the release's checksums.txt gives

column3: the fields of Kubernetes' security context types at the cluster's minor, read from k8s.io/api's core/v1/types.go; Renovate ignores tests/, no datasource reads a list of fields, and nothing fails while it is stale
column4: when versions.yaml's kubernetes moves to a new minor, read core/v1/types.go at that minor's k8s.io/api release and rewrite the list and its header

column3: an upstream dashboard file committed in this tree and loaded from a ConfigMap, so no manager has a version to read in it; the record is the release of VictoriaLogs whose dashboards directory it was taken from, which is the release the pinned chart deploys
column4: when the victoria-logs chart moves to a VictoriaLogs release, fetch dashboards/victorialogs.json of that release from the Source line, replace dashboards/victorialogs.json, and set the record, the Source line and the SHA-256 in the same pull request (docs/kubernetes.md, Dashboards)

column3: an upstream dashboard file committed in this tree and loaded from a ConfigMap, so no manager has a version to read in it; the record is the openbao chart release whose grafana/dashboards directory it was taken from, which is the release the openbao application pins
column4: when Renovate moves the openbao chart, fetch grafana/dashboards/dashboard.json of the new release from the Source line, replace dashboards/openbao.json, and set the record, the Source line and the SHA-256 in the same pull request (docs/kubernetes.md, Dashboards)

column3: the age release the etcd snapshot job downloads, an environment variable's value that no manager reads; no public image carries age, so the job fetches the release archive, and the checksums that follow it are of that archive
column4: set with the age pin in mise.toml, which tests/etcd-snapshots.bats holds it to: AGE_VERSION, then AGE_SHA256_AMD64 and AGE_SHA256_ARM64 from the new release's published linux-amd64 and linux-arm64 archives (sha256sum of each), in the same pull request
